🧠 Five biases that could cloud your next trade

Losses can shake confidence, while biases distort how you read the market. Spot them to make better decisions.

🟢 1. Recency: Recent events loom large. Zoom out; don’t let your last trade dictate the next.
🟢 2. Confirmation: You may favor analysis that supports your position and ignore opposing signals. Seek other views.
🟢 3. Herding: Don’t change a trade just because others disagree. Follow your plan; treat sentiment as context.
🟢 4. Attribution: Taking credit for wins and blaming losses on external factors hides habits to improve. Journal expectations, outcomes and lessons. Trading psychologist Dr. Brett Steenbarger says this can reveal strengths and weaknesses.
🟢 5. Addiction: Memories of big wins aren’t a reason to trade again. Check that the numbers support the setup.
